accuracyFacts: ECMAScript 2026 requires conforming hosts to support JSON modules when the request has the type attribute with value json; runtime version and deployment support still matter.

A static import/export module name may be an IdentifierName or a StringLiteral; string-literal names can expose otherwise non-identifier export names and must be aliased to a binding identifier when imported.
Import attribute keys must be unique within a with clause; duplicate keys are syntax errors. Duplicate imported local binding names are also syntax errors.
Duplicate export names are syntax errors; star-export ambiguity is resolved during export-name resolution and does not use arbitrary source order.
The module namespace object is non-extensible with a null prototype, exposes export names in sorted order, and uses exotic operations to keep exports live while rejecting writes.
Static import declarations are module-top-level syntax. Dynamic import is an expression returning a promise for a module namespace object.
ECMAScript defines linking and evaluation but delegates mapping/fetching of specifiers and import.meta properties to host integration points.
